title: Use-after-free: closures captured dangling with-env pointer
summary: WITH_END freed with-env EnvRecord while closures created inside with blocks held captured references, causing null pointer crashes on closure invocation.
why: Silent memory safety violation. Crashes only on closure call, making root cause hard to trace. Pre-existing latent bug found only via test execution.
quote: WITH_END was freeing the with-env EnvRecord via libc::free on scope exit. Closures created inside the `with` block captured act.var_env (pointing to this env record) via the CLOSURE opcode, leaving a dangling pointer.

title: Memory leak: Heap.destroy never freed HStrings or CompiledFunctions (90GB+ blowup)
summary: Heap.destroy only freed string table bucket array, not individual HStrings. CompiledFunctions never tracked. Each test leaked all objects, unbounded growth.
why: Silent memory growth - no error. 90GB+ accumulated silently until process hit OOM. Only discovered when test suite limits reached.
quote: Heap.destroy was not freeing individual HString objects in the open-addressed string table (only the bucket array), and CompiledFunction objects allocated by the compiler were never tracked or freed. Each batch_test_vm test created a fresh heap that leaked all its strings and compiled functions, causing unbounded memory growth.

title: Comparison aliasing: LT/LE/GT/GE clobbered operand before reading it
summary: Arithmetic opcodes wrote result to ra before reading rb/rc. When ra aliased rb, set_boolean clobbered the source operand, always yielding false.
why: Silent wrong values - all comparisons with register aliasing broke. Broke all for-loops. Fundamental control flow silently broken.
quote: When ra aliases rb (e.g. LE r1 = r1, r2), set_boolean(false) clobbered the source operand before the comparison, always yielding false. This broke all for-loops and any comparison where the result register matched an input register.

title: RET/RETUNDEF direct dispatch caused bytecode corruption and non-deterministic crashes
summary: Direct dispatch re-entered opcode loop without restoring valstack_top. GC collected objects with cached IC entry pointers. Non-deterministic Unknown opcode crashes.
why: Memory corruption and non-determinism - same bytecode crashed unpredictably. Silent heap corruption violated GC safety invariants.
quote: GC could collect objects whose pointers were still cached in IC entries because valstack_top wasn't properly restored for the caller, causing mark_activations to miss live registers.

title: GC mark runs with uninitialized activation fields
summary: Activation incremented activation_count before fields (var_env, lex_env, this_binding) initialized, making incomplete activations visible to GC while holding garbage pointers.
why: GC corruption: mark phase followed garbage EnvRecord pointers left from previous calls, corrupting heap during allocation.
quote: Incremented activation_count before env_create_function_scope, making activation visible to vm_mark_activations while var_env/lex_env held stale pointers from reused slot. This caused GC to follow garbage EnvRecord->bindings pointers.

title: PUTPROP setter silently corrupts caller local variables
summary: PUTPROP staged setter frame at arbitrary live local registers A..A+3, silently corrupting caller variables on return. propertyHelper broke on every accessor.
why: Silent engine-wide corruption: any code calling setters corrupted function locals. Manifested only with accessors, making it a delayed time-bomb.
quote: PUTPROP's A/B/C are arbitrary live locals, so invoking any JS setter from inside a function silently corrupted caller variables (test262 propertyHelper verifyWritable broke on every accessor property).

title: Double-free via GC allocation loop crashes
summary: Periodic GC in Heap.alloc/realloc ran inline mark-and-sweep while objects were held only in C3 locals, causing nondeterministic double-free crashes.
why: Memory corruption: C3 locals with refcount 0 were freed during inline GC before being anchored, violating engine assumption that GC never runs inline in builtins.
quote: Periodic GC in Heap.alloc/realloc was running mark-and-sweep inline, which could free objects still held only in C3 locals (refcount 0, not yet anchored). This caused nondeterministic double-free crashes in FixedBlockPool.

title: Heap.reset leaks stale pointers into freed memory
summary: Heap.reset left error_value, yield_value, iterator_symbol, toprimitive_symbol caches that survived reset and pointed into freed string-table and pool memory.
why: Use-after-free landmine: stale caches pointed to freed memory, corrupting later operations when dereferenced.
quote: Heap.reset: clear error_value, yield_value, lj.value1/value2 TVal fields and iterator_symbol/toprimitive_symbol HString* caches that survive reset and point into freed pool/string-table memory.

title: Uncaught JS exceptions silently converted to VM_ERROR crash
summary: When vm_throw_value returned false (no catcher found), 50+ opcode handlers returned VM_ERROR directly, dropping the thrown value. Engine crashed with 'execute failed: vm::VM_ERROR' + dump; actual exception never surfaced (x is not defined shown as crash instead of ReferenceError).
why: Total masking of exception messages; all uncaught exceptions appeared as VM_ERROR crashes; broken error reporting across entire engine; memory-safety landmine in error paths.
quote: all uncaught exceptions (x = 1; print(x); → 'ReferenceError: x is not defined' was thrown but never surfaced); the 50+ opcode handlers...just returned VM_ERROR~ directly, dropping the thrown value

title: Premature free of bound arguments causes heap corruption
summary: builtin_bound_call copied bound args without incref before re-dispatch, causing net over-decref when args are heap values. Pool block recycled into next bound function, corrupting .name property.
why: Memory safety: over-decref leads to premature free and pool reuse, silently corrupting heap objects. Affects every bound-function-with-object-args pattern.
quote: The result was a net over-decref: a heap value passed as a bound argument (e.g. a TypedArray constructor via `factory.bind(undefined, Float64Array)`) was freed while still live. Its pool block was then recycled into the next bound function, whose `.name = "bound <target>"` write corrupted the original object

title: Silent string comparison failures due to missing interning
summary: String concatenation fast path (ra aliases source) produced un-interned HStrings. Engine equality (SEQ, indexOf, includes, property keys) is pointer identity on interned strings. Un-interned results that escaped compared unequal to identical literals: cat4.indexOf('(())') returned -1 while cat4[0] === '(())' was true.
why: Silent wrong values in idiomatic code; no error raised; comparison broken by optimization; discovered after moveelim activated aliased ADD
quote: The skip-intern accumulator fast path (ra aliases a source register) produced un-interned HStrings... String equality across the engine... is pointer identity on the interned HString, so an un-interned concat result that escapes... compares unequal to the interned literal with the same contents: cat4.indexOf('(())') returned -1 while cat4[0] === '(())' was true.

title: Two latent bugs in Array.fromAsync unmasked by channel fix
summary: Bugs were false-passes before ef32064: channel leak silently swallowed test rejections. (1) Symbols wrapped with string_proto instead of symbol_proto, causing wrong array-like path. (2) Prologue throws clobbered ctx.result, returning undefined instead of rejected promise.
why: Pre-existing silent bugs masked by another bug; tests never caught them; revealed only after channel leak fix
quote: Both were false-passes before ef32064: the stale-channel leak it fixed was silently swallowing these tests' rejections. A Symbol primitive wrapped for the array-like path got string_proto... so fromAsync found String.prototype[@@iterator] and rejected... instead of using Symbol.prototype array-like reads.

title: Multiple large-string memory leaks and UAF in VM
summary: Large non-interned strings lack mark-sweep backstop; any register write clobbering the last owned reference leaked permanently. Found in resolve_call_var/global (borrowed fast paths), ADD/ADDI concat (untracked), RET write-back, LDINT/INC/DEC/NEWOBJ slow paths, and free_catcher_chain (leaked try-Catchers). Measured ~2000 objects per workload.
why: Multiple independent leak paths in hot codepaths; measured at 2000→15 object leaks; silent accumulation without bounds
quote: Large non-interned strings... are pure refcounted leaves with no string-table or mark-sweep backstop: any register write that clobbers the last owned reference leaks the block permanently. Measured with `leaks --atExit`: call-result string 2015→15, discarded-result 2015→15, concat-into-number 2015→15, return-from-try Catcher 5015→15

title: Dangling pointer in private-name table realloc
summary: Each CompilerContext held its own copy of private-name storage (entries, count, cap). When a borrowing context reallocated the shared entries buffer during growth, it left owner and sibling borrowers with stale pointers into freed memory. The 65th private name triggered the first realloc past initial cap of 64, causing aliasing or crashes.
why: Use-after-free via stale pointers to freed private-name storage; silent aliasing until 65+ names trigger realloc
quote: each CompilerContext held its own copy of the (entries, count, cap) triple. When a borrowing context... declared private names via a nested class in a field initializer, it grew its OWN copy and reallocated the shared entries buffer — leaving the owner and every sibling borrower with a stale pointer into freed memory. The 65th private name (first realloc past the initial cap of 64) therefore aliased or crashed

title: Async GeneratorState memory leak and use-after-free crash
summary: resume_fn and reject_fn closures in async functions both referenced the same GeneratorState but neither owned it; hobject_free never freed it, causing 100% leak of all suspended async functions and crashing when GC tried to free untracked reaction chains.
why: Memory safety catastrophe: segfault on GC + permanent leaks. Pre-existing, undetected by tests.
quote: hobject_free never freed this GS at all, leaking the struct (and its saved_regs/this_binding) on every async function that suspends at least once... the baseline binary (4fe6cfe9) segfaults outright on the same completed-2000 repro once a full mark-and-sweep pass runs, from the reaction-chain `.next` bug

title: Proxy own-keys trap use-after-free on garbage collection
summary: Proxy partitioned_own_keys trap result array collected during [[GetOwnProperty]] re-entry due to temproot clear at safepoint. Segfaults on 50+ key proxies under GC pressure.
why: Memory safety: use-after-free of array during iteration. ASAN reports use-after-poison in HObject.array_part; without ASAN causes exit 139.
quote: The array was reachable only from a C3 local the mark phase cannot see, so it was collected partway through the loop and the next arr.array_part()[i] read freed memory. ASAN reports use-after-poison in HObject.array_part; without ASAN a 50-key proxy for-in under GC pressure segfaults (exit 139).

title: RegExp global flag ignored: lastIndex never updated, infinite loops
summary: RegExp exec/test ignored global flag and lastIndex property, always starting from position 0, causing infinite loops in global matching patterns.
why: Silent wrong behavior - idiomatic global matching patterns hung instead of terminating. No error raised. Pre-existing feature gap.
quote: Previously, exec/test always started matching from position 0, ignoring lastIndex. This caused infinite loops in do...while patterns that iterate over global matches (6 hanging RegExp tests now pass).

title: is_truthy silently treated FASTINT 0 and empty strings as truthy
summary: is_truthy macro only checked UNDEFINED/NULL/BOOLEAN, causing FASTINT 0 and empty strings to return true. while(0) and while(\"\") became infinite loops.
why: Silent wrong values for core falsiness check. Idiomatic loops hung instead of exiting, revealing nothing about root cause.
quote: The NaNBox is_truthy macro only handled UNDEFINED, NULL, and BOOLEAN (false) as falsy. FASTINT 0 and empty STRING fell through to return true, causing infinite loops in while(0), while(\"\"), do-while(0), etc.

title: Member assignment lhs_mode clobber: bracket notation compiled to GETPROP
summary: expression() inside bracket handler reset lhs_mode to false. obj[key] = value compiled to GETPROP instead of PUTPROP, silently losing assignment.
why: Silent wrong behavior - assignment silently became read-only. No error raised. Fundamental language feature broken.
quote: The inner expression() call inside the bracket handler of member_expr() calls assignment_expr(), which resets lhs_mode to false. This clobbered the outer lhs_mode=true state needed for PUTPROP emission.

title: for-of continue infinite loop: continue_target pointed to comparison
summary: for-of continue_target set to LT comparison instead of increment. continue re-entered same iteration without advancing index.
why: Pre-existing latent bug in ES6 feature. for-of with continue silently hangs. Test suite never caught this edge case.
quote: continue_target was set to the LT comparison, causing continue to re-enter the same iteration without advancing the index.
